items.title: Konitz Lee — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: totally immersed in his ideas of how to do things and I wanted to find out how to do them from my own perspective. All through the years I have been doing that in my way, trying to make it as meaningful as possible, giving full credit to his inspiration. But as I listen to Ted Brown still playing, I heard him the other night playing differently and I was knocked out. He was actually leaving rests and not just pouring out the “eighth-note boogie”. It was obviously Lester Young-influenced, the rests and some…

Yeah. They started out with this tune at this tempo [taps a fast tempo] and [on] some other tunes I’ve heard Warne with Niels Henning and Al Levitt playing very fast tempos very flawlessly. Do you know the book this man in Australia wrote?
